test_cases.title: Scenario File Format - Human Editable Inspection
test_cases.setup: Checkout repository at the FT1 baseline tag. Open the scenario file directory under sim/sim_scenario/scenarios/ in a text editor.
procedure: Open the FT1 baseline scenario file in a plain text editor.
Inspect the file for human-readable structured text (e.g., YAML/JSON/Trick input syntax) without binary content.
Modify a scalar parameter (e.g., launch elevation), save, and re-run the loader to confirm the change is consumed.
Verify the file is tracked in git and produces a readable diff when modified.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Scenario file is plain text, hand-editable, produces a readable diff under git, and edits are picked up by the loader without recompilation.

test_cases.title: Launch Site Latitude/Longitude/Elevation Loading
test_cases.setup: Construct a SimScenario instance pointing at a fixture scenario file with known launch site values (lat=34.0522, lon=-118.2437, elev=89.0 m).
procedure: Call SimScenario_Load() on the fixture scenario file.
Read back launch site latitude, longitude, and elevation via the scenario API.
Compare each retrieved value against the fixture's known value within 1e-6 deg / 1e-3 m tolerance.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Loaded launch site latitude, longitude, and elevation match the fixture file within tolerance.

test_cases.title: Motor Thrust Curve Time-Indexed Loading
test_cases.setup: Fixture scenario file references a known motor thrust curve (e.g., G-class with at least 5 sample points spanning 0 s to burnout).
procedure: Call SimScenario_Load() on the fixture file.
Retrieve the motor thrust curve sample array via the scenario API.
Verify each (time, thrust) sample matches the fixture data point-for-point.
Verify the curve sample count and total burn duration match expected values.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Loaded thrust curve samples and burn duration match the fixture's time-indexed motor data exactly.

test_cases.title: Vehicle Mass and Drag Parameter Loading
test_cases.setup: Fixture scenario file specifies known dry mass, propellant mass, reference area, and Cd values.
procedure: Call SimScenario_Load() on the fixture file.
Retrieve dry mass, propellant mass, reference area, and drag coefficient via the scenario API.
Compare each value to the fixture-known value within 1e-6 relative tolerance.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Loaded mass and drag parameters match the fixture-specified values within tolerance.

test_cases.title: Atmosphere Pressure/Temperature/Wind Loading
test_cases.setup: Fixture scenario file specifies sea-level pressure (e.g., 101325 Pa), surface temperature (e.g., 288.15 K), and a wind vector (e.g., 5 m/s, bearing 270 deg).
procedure: Call SimScenario_Load() on the fixture file.
Retrieve pressure, temperature, and wind vector via the scenario API.
Compare each value to the fixture-known value within 1e-3 absolute tolerance.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Loaded atmospheric pressure, temperature, and wind components match the fixture file within tolerance.

test_cases.title: Per-Sensor Noise and Bias Parameter Loading
test_cases.setup: Fixture scenario file specifies distinct noise sigma and bias values for IMU accel, IMU gyro, baro pressure, and GPS position.
procedure: Call SimScenario_Load() on the fixture file.
Retrieve IMU accel, IMU gyro, baro, and GPS noise and bias parameters via the scenario API.
Verify each retrieved sigma and bias matches the fixture-specified value exactly.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Loaded per-sensor noise sigma and bias values match the fixture-specified values for IMU, baro, and GPS.

test_cases.title: Truth State Sidecar File Created During Run
test_cases.setup: Configure SimScenario to run a short (1 s) integration with truth-output enabled at a temporary directory.
procedure: Run the simulation for a fixed wall duration with the truth-output path set.
After the run, check the temporary directory for the truth state sidecar file.
Open the sidecar file and verify it is non-empty and contains state columns (position, velocity, attitude).
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Truth state sidecar file exists, is non-empty, and contains the expected state columns after the simulation run.

test_cases.title: Truth Recording at Integration Rate
test_cases.setup: Configure scenario with a known integration step (e.g., dt=1 ms) and run for exactly 1.000 s of sim time.
procedure: Run the simulation for 1.000 s sim time with truth output enabled.
Count the number of truth state records in the sidecar file.
Compute deltas between consecutive timestamps and check the median delta against the integration step.
Verify the record count equals integration steps within +/- 1.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Median timestamp delta across all truth-state records equals the configured integration dt within an absolute tolerance of 1e-9 s; record count matches the expected (run_duration_s / dt) value within +/-1 record.

test_cases.title: Monotonic Simulation Time Stamps in Truth Records
test_cases.setup: Run the FT1 baseline scenario for at least 2 s of sim time with truth output enabled.
procedure: Open the truth state sidecar file produced by the run.
Iterate through all records and compare each timestamp to the previous timestamp.
Verify every timestamp is strictly greater than its predecessor.
Verify the first timestamp equals 0 (or a configured t0) within 1e-9 s.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All truth state timestamps are strictly monotonically increasing across the entire run.

test_cases.title: True Phase Transition Timestamps Recorded
test_cases.setup: Run the FT1 baseline scenario through a complete flight (boost, coast, apogee, descent) with truth output enabled.
procedure: Run the full FT1 baseline scenario to landing.
Open the truth phase-transition record (or sidecar phase log).
Verify entries exist for boost-to-coast, coast-to-apogee, and apogee-to-descent transitions.
Verify each recorded transition time is non-decreasing and lies within the simulation time range.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Truth phase transition log contains a timestamp for every flight phase transition produced during the run, in non-decreasing order.

test_cases.title: FT1 Baseline Scenario Default Inspection
test_cases.setup: Locate the FT1 baseline scenario file under sim/sim_scenario/scenarios/.
procedure: Open the FT1 baseline scenario file.
Inspect the motor reference and confirm it is a G-class motor.
Inspect the noise parameter block and confirm sigmas are at the documented nominal values.
Run the baseline scenario and verify simulated apogee falls within 600 m +/- 50 m using the truth state file.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Baseline scenario specifies a G-class motor with nominal noise parameters and produces an apogee within 600 m +/- 50 m.

test_cases.title: Trick CLI Scenario Selection
test_cases.setup: Two scenario files exist: ft1_baseline (G-motor, nominal noise) and a variant (different motor or wind). Trick S_main launcher is built.
procedure: Launch the simulator with --scenario=ft1_baseline and capture the loaded-scenario log line.
Launch the simulator with --scenario=<variant> and capture the loaded-scenario log line.
Compare loaded scenario name and selected motor/wind identifiers between the two runs.
Verify each run loaded the scenario indicated on the command line without rebuilding.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Each Trick invocation loads the scenario named on the CLI argument, with identifying parameters matching the chosen file.

test_cases.title: Human-Editable Round-Trip Preservation
test_cases.setup: Copy the FT1 baseline scenario file to a temporary working directory. Construct a SimScenario instance pointing at the copied file.
procedure: Call SimScenario_Load() on the unmodified copied baseline scenario file and capture all parsed parameter values into a reference struct.
Open the copied scenario file in a text editor and modify only a comment line (or insert a new comment line) such that no semantic content changes.
Save the edited scenario file and call SimScenario_Load() again on the same path, capturing the parsed parameter values into a second struct.
Compare every field of the second parsed struct to the reference struct using bitwise equality.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All loaded parameter values are bitwise identical before and after a comment-only edit, confirming the format is human-editable without affecting semantics.

test_cases.title: Truth State Columns Schema Verification
test_cases.setup: Run the FT1 baseline for at least 100 ms of sim time with truth output enabled.
procedure: Open the produced truth sidecar file.
Inspect the header row and confirm columns include sim_time, position (x,y,z), velocity (x,y,z), and attitude (quaternion).
Parse one record and verify all numeric columns are finite (no NaN/Inf).
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Truth sidecar contains the documented schema (sim_time, position, velocity, attitude) and all numeric values are finite.
